newsitem.title: UK: Ryanair to acquire six Lufthansa B-737s.
newsitem.headline: Ryanair to acquire six Lufthansa B-737s.

text.p: Irish low-cost airline Ryanair said on Tuesday that it has agreed to buy six Boeing Co 737-200s from German carrier Deutsche Lufthansa AG in a deal valued at $60 million, to equip expansion from London into mainland Europe.
The airline said in a statement that the deal is being financed by a mixture of company funds and a loan facility from a consortium of Irish banks.
Ryanair said it will take delivery of the first aircraft next week with the others following next year, to increase its total fleet to 17 B-737s.

"We are delighted to announce this order as it is the completion of many months of negotiations and secures Ryanair's fleet development program for the next two years," commercial director Tim Jeans said. "We intend to base these additional aircraft at (London's) Stansted airport and...will enable Ryanair to develop a range of low fare services from Stansted to European destinations over the coming years."

In August the family-owned company sold a 20 percent stake in the airline to Irish Air LP, a group of private investors led by Texan entrepreneur David Bonderman, chairman of Continental Airlines Inc.
